extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians (job applicants, departments/advertisers submitting classifieds, and readers of Notices of the AMS)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for placing classified advertisements in the Notices of the AMS and for preparing/submitting academic job (faculty/postdoc/editor) applications to departments and AMS offices. Covers ad rates/format, submission/payment, and application materials, deadlines, and selection criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classified advertising rates
rubrics_metrics.description: The 1992 rate is $60 per inch on a single column (one-inch minimum), calculated from the top of the type; $30 for each additional if.;. inch or fraction thereof. No discounts for multiple ads or the same ad in consecutive issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any fractional text will be charged at the next inch rate. For an additional $10 charge, announcements can be placed anonymously (correspondence will be forwarded). All prices subject to change. Free shipment by surface; for air delivery, add $6.50 per title (for book orders). Prepayment required of individuals but not of institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classified ad formatting and headline rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertisements in the 'Positions Available' classified section will be set with a minimum one-line headline, consisting of the institution name above body copy, unless additional headline copy is specified by the advertiser. Headlines will be centered in boldface at no extra charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertisements in other sections of the classified pages will be set according to the advertisement insertion. Classified rates are calculated from top of type in headline to bottom of type in body copy, including lines and spaces within. Ads will appear in the language in which they are submitted. Dictation over the telephone will not be accepted for classified advertising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classified ad submission, payment, and contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Send ad and check to: Advertising Department, AMS, P. O. Box 6248, Providence, Rhode Island 02940. AMS location for express delivery packages is 201 Charles Street, Providence, Rhode Island 02904. Individuals are requested to pay in advance, institutions are not required to do so. AMS FAX 401-455-4004.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepayment is required of individuals but not of institutions. Deadlines are listed on the inside front cover or may be obtained from the AMS Advertising Department. No member discounts for classified ads. For additional information (e.g., anonymous placement, free situations-wanted rules) call the AMS Advertising Department or the provided toll-free number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and insertion policy
rubrics_metrics.description: DEADLINES are listed on the inside front cover or may be obtained from the AMS Advertising Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No discounts for multiple ads or the same ad in consecutive issues. Ads will be set according to insertion; fractional text charged at next inch. Late insertions subject to availability and the stated policies of the Advertising Department.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Situations wanted' acceptance policy
rubrics_metrics.description: SITUATIONS WANTED ADVERTISEMENTS from involuntarily unemployed mathematicians are accepted under certain conditions for free publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call toll-free 800-321-4AMS (321-4267) in the U.S. and Canada for further information about eligibility/conditions for free publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-discrimination statement requirement for foreign employers
rubrics_metrics.description: U. S. LAWS PROHIBIT discrimination in employment on the basis of color, age, sex, race, religion or national origin. 'Positions Available' advertisements from institutions outside the U. S. cannot be published unless they are accompanied by a statement that the institution does not discriminate on these grounds whether or not it is subject to U. S. laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details and specific wording may be found near the Classified Advertisements in the January and July/August issues of the Notices. Advertisers should include the required wording when submitting ads from outside the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard application materials requested (CV, publications, reprints, statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should forward a curriculum vitae, a list of publications, and a small number of reprints and/or preprints (or equivalents). Many advertised positions request also a letter of interest, a statement describing current and planned research, and any appropriate material about teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific adverts require variations: e.g., 'send a vita, list of publications, and a statement describing current and planned research' (Carnegie Mellon/Postdoc listings), or 'a letter stating one's professional aims, a resume, graduate and undergraduate transcripts, and three recommendations' for some liberal-arts colleges. Provide the materials requested in the ad and conform to any page/format instructions if given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of recommendation — number and focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertised positions typically require arrange for at least three letters of recommendation to be forwarded; some Canadian/other positions request four letters. At least one letter should deal primarily with the candidate's teaching in some listings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should arrange that referees send letters directly to the named contact. Failure to provide the requested number or type (e.g., one letter chiefly about teaching) may affect consideration. Some ads specify a minimum (three) or four letters; follow the specific ad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcripts for non-faculty applicants or junior applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who do not hold a current, full time faculty appointment as indicated on the resume must also submit transcripts. Junior applicants (e.g., 'junior applicants only') are asked to submit transcripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where requested, include graduate and undergraduate transcripts with the application. This is often required to verify degrees or for early-career candidates who lack extensive faculty appointments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria — demonstrated excellence in research and teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection is based on demonstration and promise of excellence in research, teaching, and innovative applications. Senior candidates are expected to have demonstrated leadership in research; junior candidates should show promise beyond the doctoral dissertation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include 'preference to applicants with postdoctoral experience who have made substantial research contributions beyond the doctoral dissertation' and expectations of 'strong commitment to high quality undergraduate and graduate teaching.' Provide evidence of research productivity, teaching commitment, and potential impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research/field fit and departmental needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments list preferred fields to complement but not duplicate existing research strengths (examples: arithmetic geometry, computational science, dynamical systems, differential geometry, nonlinear science, number theory, probability, PDEs, geometric analysis, applied mathematics areas, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertised listings often state specific areas of interest and may exclude other areas (e.g., Johns Hopkins: 'Applicants whose primary research is in algebra, analysis, geometry, logic, number theory, or topology will not be considered'). Tailor applications to the stated departmental needs and explicitly explain fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to work and citizenship/immigration priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Hiring is contingent upon eligibility to work in the United States. For Canadian universities, priority will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents in accordance with immigration requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, include documentation or make your eligibility clear; foreign applicants may need to obtain appropriate visas or satisfy immigration priorities. Ads often state that hiring is contingent on eligibility to work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application deadlines and consideration windows
rubrics_metrics.description: Many ads provide a date by which 'to ensure full consideration' applications should be received (examples: 'Full consideration will be given to candidates whose materials arrive by December 31, 1992', 'Applications are requested by January 15, 1993', 'The deadline for application is January 20, 1993').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some ads note that late applications may be considered 'until the positions are filled' or 'on a space-available basis.' To maximize consideration, submit by the stated deadline and follow any guidance about 'first consideration' dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral appointment conditions and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-doctoral fellowships (research associates) are often one-year appointments (twelve-month) joint appointments, with at most one course taught per semester; applicants should send a vita, list of publications, a statement describing current and planned research, and arrange for at least three letters of recommendation. Deadlines specified (e.g., January 20, 1993).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These positions may include special awards (e.g., 'Center of Excellence Awards in nonlinear optics and fluid mechanics') and sometimes allow late applications 'on a space-available basis.' Teaching load and appointment length are specified; follow those when considering suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Named/targeted appointments — reduced teaching load and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Named assistant professorships (e.g., Zeev Nehari, Richard J. Duffin) may carry reduced academic-year teaching loads (example: six hours per week during one semester and three hours per week during the other), be for one- or two-year initial periods extendable by agreement, and expect exceptional research promise and evidence of achievement with research interests intersecting current faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants for such positions should send a vita, list of publications, a research statement, and arrange for three letters of recommendation, addressing how their research intersects department strengths and how they meet the reduced-load/expectation profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department head/chair selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates for Head will be filled by a person with an outstanding record of achievement in research and teaching and with demonstrable administrative skills. Effective communication, a talent for management, and ability to provide visionary leadership are especially important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications typically request a resume and names of references; selection emphasizes both academic stature and administrative/leadership abilities. Prepare documentation demonstrating prior leadership, management experience, and vision for the department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Reviews (MR) Associate Editor responsibilities and qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibilities: selecting articles and books suitable for review, classifying items, assigning them to reviewers, editing reviews when returned, and correcting galley proofs. Qualifications: individual with considerable breadth in pure or applied mathematics is sought; preference given to those with expertise in numerical analysis; the ability to write good English is essential and the ability to read mathematics in major foreign languages (Russian or Chinese especially desirable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointments are one- or two-year half-time positions; salary negotiable and commensurate with experience. Applicants should submit a curriculum vitae, bibliography, and names/addresses of at least three references. Persons combining a sabbatical or leave with this appointment are encouraged to inquire.
